title: How to change cursor in Xcode on Mac: System settings and multi-cursor editing explained
metaTitle: How to change cursor in Xcode on Mac: Simple Settings Guide
description: Learn how to change cursor on Mac to affect Xcode. Discover how to customize system pointer settings and master multi-cursor editing in Xcode 27.
targetKeyword: how to change cursor on mac
intro: You cannot change the mouse cursor appearance specifically within the Xcode application interface. Xcode relies on macOS system-wide settings to determine the shape, size, and color of your pointer.
tldr: Xcode uses the standard macOS system cursor for all interactions.
Adjust your cursor size and color in System Settings > Accessibility > Display > Pointer.
Use multi-cursor editing in Xcode by holding Control + Shift and clicking to add insertion points.
Hold Option and drag to perform column selection in your code files.

blocks.text: Why you cannot change the cursor inside Xcode

Xcode is a native macOS application built using Apple frameworks. It follows the system human interface guidelines strictly. Unlike web-based editors that allow custom CSS for cursor styling, Xcode does not provide a setting to modify the pointer icon or behavior locally. When you move your mouse into the Xcode window, it inherits the properties defined in your macOS System Settings.
How to change cursor on Mac system wide

To change the cursor appearance, you must adjust the system settings. These changes apply to Xcode and every other app on your machine. Follow these steps to improve visibility or personalize your pointer.

items: Click the Apple menu in the top left corner of your screen.
Select System Settings from the dropdown menu.
Navigate to the Accessibility tab in the sidebar.
Locate the Pointer settings at the bottom of the window.
Adjust the Pointer size slider to your preferred scale.
Click the Pointer outline color or Pointer fill color swatches to pick a new shade.

blocks.text: If you are using an older version of macOS, such as Monterey, this menu is found in System Preferences instead of System Settings. The path remains similar, focusing on the Accessibility and Display panels.

While you cannot change the visual appearance of the pointer, you can change how the text cursor functions within the editor. Xcode supports multi-cursor editing, which is useful when you need to change the same variable name or syntax across multiple lines simultaneously.

items: To add multiple insertion points, hold the Control (⌃) and Shift (⇧) keys, then click in the editor where you want each cursor to appear.
To select a vertical block of text, hold the Option (⌥) key and drag your mouse across the lines you wish to modify.
Use the arrow keys while holding Control (⌃) and Shift (⇧) to extend your current selection to adjacent lines.
Press the Escape (⎋) key to clear all additional cursors and return to a single insertion point.

blocks.text: Common mistakes when customizing your workspace

Many developers look for third-party tools to force a custom cursor style inside Xcode. This is generally discouraged. Tools that modify system-level cursor behavior can interfere with macOS Security and Integrity Protection. You might find that your custom cursor disappears during system updates or causes lag when the IDE performs heavy indexing tasks.

Another common error is assuming the I-beam cursor can be modified independently of the standard arrow pointer. macOS treats the text insertion point as a system-wide resource. If you increase the pointer size, the I-beam will also scale proportionally. This can sometimes make the I-beam appear too thick for fine code editing. If this happens, return to the Accessibility settings and reduce the size until you find a balance that works for your screen resolution.

Beyond cursor settings, your productivity in Xcode depends on how you navigate the IDE. Use keyboard shortcuts to reduce the need for mouse movement entirely. For instance, Command (⌘) + Shift (⇧) + O opens the Open Quickly dialog, allowing you to jump to any file without touching the navigator.

If you find yourself constantly moving your mouse to locate the cursor, enable the Shake mouse pointer to locate feature in the same Accessibility menu. When you wiggle your trackpad or mouse, the pointer will briefly expand, making it easy to spot on large or high-resolution displays.

faq.question: Can I change the cursor color only for Xcode?
faq.answer: No. Cursor settings in macOS are global and apply to every application, including Xcode.

faq.question: How do I add multiple cursors in Xcode?
faq.answer: Hold Control (⌃) + Shift (⇧) and click anywhere in your code to place additional insertion points.

faq.question: Where is the cursor setting in macOS?
faq.answer: Go to System Settings > Accessibility > Display > Pointer.

task: Change the cursor appearance on your Mac to affect the Xcode environment.

steps.name: Open System Settings
steps.text: Click the Apple menu in the top left corner of your screen and select System Settings.

steps.name: Access Accessibility
steps.text: In the sidebar, click on Accessibility to view your system interaction settings.

steps.name: Configure Pointer
steps.text: Select Display, then scroll to the bottom to find the Pointer options.

steps.name: Adjust Settings
steps.text: Move the slider to change the pointer size or click the color swatches to change the fill and outline colors.
steps.tip: Enable the shake to locate feature if you often lose track of your cursor.

troubleshooting.problem: The cursor is too large for code editing.
troubleshooting.fix: Return to System Settings > Accessibility > Display > Pointer and reduce the size slider.
Ensure you are holding both Control and Shift before clicking in the editor.
